title: Austin: Underground Wires, Bar Signs, Speeding Fines
summary:
*   **Modernizing Communications:** Austin pushes for modernizing its telephone system, requiring the Southwestern Telegraph and Telephone Company to install underground conduits for its wires.
*   **Vibrant Business Scene:** Greenlights unique business permits, including an illuminated "Drinks" sign at 2107 Speedway and a custom tiled walkway for the Crystal Bar and Cafe on Congress Avenue.
*   **Early Auto Regulation & Discretion:** Remits half the fine for a "youth" caught speeding in an automobile, noting it was their first offense.
*   **Essential City Upgrades:** Approves street improvements for Guadalupe and 19th streets, and allocates funds for three years of fire insurance for City Hall and city fire stations.

Oct 24th 1913.

The Council was called to order by the Mayor with all members present: The Mayor laid
before the Council the following resolution: Whereas, the application of W H Stephens to
install and maintain in this City ,is recommended by the City Electrical Inspector ,Mr W L
Eyres, as per attached written recommendation; Now, Therefore , Be it resolved by the City
Council of the City of Austin : W.H. Stephens That the petition of W H Stephens be and is
hereby granted ,and he is hereby authorized to establish and maintain at 2107Speedway,an
electric light sign , with the words " Drinks" in illumination thereon .
Be it further resolved:
That this permit be and is hereby declared to be revocable at the pleasure of the City
Council .
The resolution was adopted by the following vote : Yeas Mayor Wooldridge, Councilmen
Anthony,Bartholomew ,Haynes & Powell 5 Nays none.
Approved _____________________Mayor.
The Council then recessed subject to call. October 25th 1913.
The Council was called to order by the Mayor with all members present,except Councilman

tile walkway
Be it resolved by the City Council of the City of Austin : That permit be and is hereby
granted to Al Watkins , proprietor of the Crystal Bar and Cafe, situated at 706, Congress
Avenue, to construct and maintain under the supervision of the City Engineer , and with
the approval of the Supt of Streets and Public Improvements , a tiled walkway into his
premises at said 706 Congress Avenue.
The tiled walkway hereby authorized is to be absolutely flush with the concrete pavement
through which it is laid, and to be of the width of the doorway into his said premises .
That said Al Watkins is hereby granted the right of having the words " Crystal Bar and
Cafe" worked into said walkway.
Be it further resolved :
That this permit is granted and is to be accepted as temporary and revocable at any time
in the pleasure of the City Council .
The resolution was adopted by the following vote : Yeas Mayor Wooldridge, Councilmen
Anthony, Bartholomew & Haynes 4

The Council was called to order by the Mayor with all members present: The Mayor laid
before the Council the following resolution : Be it resolved by the City Council of the
City of Austin: That A P Wooldridge, Mayor of the City of Austin, be and he is hereby
authorized Samuel Payne to enter into an agreement with Samuel Payne to arbitrate the
matter of title and value of a certain strip,tract or parcel of land in the City of
Austin, Texas described as follows : Beginning at the S W corner of Lot No 2 ,in Block No
2, of H B Seider’s addition to the City of Austin ,Travis County ,Texas, ;thence in a
southerly direction Arbitration and in the same course as the extension of the W lineof
said Lot No 2to the N line of Spring or 38th street ; thence W easterly with the N line of
said 38th street a distance of 30 1/4 feet ; thence northerly and parallelwith the said
south extension of the W line of said Lot No 2 to the intersection of the extension
westerly of the S line of said Lot No 2; thence easterly and parallel with the N line of
said Spring or 38th street 30 1/3 feet to the S W corner of said Lot No 2.
The terms and conditions upon which this agreement is entered into are not set out in the

The resolution was adopted by the following vote: Yeas Mayor Wooldridge, Councilmen
Anthony, Bartholomew, Haynes & Powell 5 Nays none.
Approved, A P Wooldridge, Mayor.

October 25th 1913:
The Council was called to order by the Mayor with all members present: Councilman Anthony
offered the following resolution : Be it resolved by the City Council of the City of
Austin : That onehalf of the fine and costs in case No 8137, State of Texas vs E Barrow E
Barrow
Fine Remitted
for exceeding the speed limit in an automobile , which onehalf of fine and costs amounts
to $ 7.40 ,be and the same is hereby accepted in full payment of the fine and costs
amounting to $ 14.80, imposed in said case.
The reason for the remission of onehalf of the fine and costs in this case is that the
said E Barrow is a mere youth and this is his first offense.
Theresolution was adopted by the following vote; Yeas Mayor Wooldridge, Councilmen
Anthony, Bartholomew, Haynes & Powell 5 Nays none.
Approved , A P Wooldridge, Mayor.
The Council then adjourned.
